problem: Prior navigation work either learns task-specific policies, assumes the environment was already explored or mapped (e.g., SPTM), or relies on hand-crafted geometric exploration such as frontier-based methods. Frontier methods break under odometry noise, cannot use semantic cues such as doors, and need accurate range sensing. Generic intrinsic-reward RL (curiosity) is sample-inefficient in realistic 3D houses. No one had learned a task-agnostic exploration policy for realistic 3D indoor environments.
motivation: Both SLAM pipelines and learning-based navigation need a way to explore a new environment first: to build a map, or to gather experience for downstream tasks. In practice this is done by a human operator, heuristics, random exploration, or GT maps. The paper observes three things. A small amount of human exploration data (EQA trajectories) can bootstrap semantic behaviour such as 'doors are pathways'. A coverage reward computable purely from on-board sensors gives a dense training signal. Learned policies can be more robust than geometry to pose noise and to mismatches between geometry and affordance.
key_idea: Learn a task-agnostic exploration policy with a recurrent network over RGB plus egocentric coarse and fine occupancy maps: first imitate human exploration trajectories, then fine-tune with PPO on an intrinsic map-coverage-gain reward plus a bump-sensor collision penalty, both computed from on-board sensors.
insight: Across all input configurations, IL pretraining on only 693 human EQA trajectories both raises coverage and sharply reduces the large run-to-run variance of pure RL; RL on coverage then improves coverage further (Fig. 3 left/center). Both RGB and map inputs contribute (Fig. 3). The dense coverage-gain reward beats an extrinsic reward from sparse 'reward-yielding objects' at 1 or 4 per m² (Fig. 3 right). The main advantage over geometric exploration is robustness, not raw coverage. With perfect pose, frontier exploration is best. Under compounding odometry noise frontier degrades rapidly, and the learned agent (trained without noise) overtakes it from about 4% noise. When doors are rendered but not collidable, frontier planning fails badly while the learned policy drops only slightly, because it has learned from demos and RL that doors are traversable.
method: Map construction: dead-reckoning pose estimate x̂_{t+1}=f(x̂_t,a_t) from a known transition model. Each depth frame is back-projected with camera intrinsics, transformed by x̂, and projected to a 2D allocentric occupancy grid at 0.05 m resolution (traversable / non-traversable / unknown). There is no bundle adjustment; learning is expected to absorb misalignment.

Policy network: three ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18s (last FC resized to 128) encode the RGB image (224→80×80), an egocentric coarse map (40m×40m at 0.5 m, 80×80), and an egocentric fine map (4m×4m at 0.05 m). Outputs are concatenated (384-d) → FC 128 → single-layer GRU (128) → policy head (128-32-6) and value head (128-32-1), with ELU activations.

Intrinsic reward: R = α·[C(M_{t+1})−C(M_t)] + β·(−Bump(t+1)), where coverage C is the number of known (free or occupied) grid cells and the bump sensor supplies the collision penalty. α=0.0005, β=0.006; extrinsic reward is 0.

Imitation bootstrap: behavioral cloning on 693 AMT human trajectories from EmbodiedQA in House3D. Questions are ignored, trajectories under 100 steps are removed, and the rest are cut into RNN-length (20) segments.
RL fine-tuning: PPO on 20 training houses from random start locations, 500-step episodes, 6400 episodes (3.2M steps), Adam lr 1e-5, entropy coefficient 0.01.

Downstream use: run the exploration policy for 1500 steps in a new house and store posed RGB images. For image-goal navigation, localize the goal by nearest-neighbour matching in ResNet-18 feature space, then plan a shortest path on the occupancy map built during exploration.

setting.backbone: 3× ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 encoders (RGB, coarse map, fine map) + GRU actor-critic, trained with behavioral cloning then PPO
setting.training_data: 693 human exploration trajectories from EmbodiedQA (AMT, House3D) for behavioral cloning, then 3.2M steps of PPO (6400 episodes × 500 steps) with intrinsic coverage reward on 20 House3D/SUNCG training houses
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (60° FOV, depth clipped at 3 m) + bump sensor + dead-reckoned pose estimate, used to build egocentric coarse and fine occupancy maps
setting.action_space: 6 discrete primitives: move forward/backward 0.25 m, strafe left/right 0.25 m, turn left/right 9°
setting.simulator: House3D (SUNCG), modified so doors are neither rendered nor collidable (except in the geometry-affordance mismatch experiment)
setting.privileged: In the main no-noise setting the map is built from ground-truth pose (x̂_t = x_t); noise experiments use noisy dead reckoning. The downstream nav experiment uses no state-estimation noise, plus a 1500-step pre-exploration of the test house.

numbers_note: Most results appear only in figures: coverage-vs-time curves (Fig. 2 left/right, Fig. 3 ablations), coverage-vs-noise curves (Fig. 2 center), and goal-image localization success-vs-threshold curves, top-1/top-5 (Fig. 4 top). None of these have numeric tables. The only explicitly printed numbers are the two 10%-noise coverage values (117.4 / 98.9 m²) and the downstream SPL (0.87 with exploration vs 0.69 without). The own method's no-noise coverage and all baseline coverage values are figure-only.
results: On 20 unseen House3D test houses, the full IL+RL Map+RGB policy out-explores random, 'straight' (robot-vacuum), curiosity-based, and RGB-only coverage-reward agents. Frontier-based exploration is best only with perfect pose. With compounding odometry noise the learned agent beats frontier from about 4% noise, reaching 117.4 m² at 10% noise, or 98.9 m² when trained with noisy rewards. It also suffers only a minor drop when doors break geometric assumptions, whereas frontier drops heavily. Using exploration data for downstream image-goal navigation raises SPL from 0.69 (no prior exploration) to 0.87, and gives better goal-image localization than random or curiosity exploration.
limitations: Simulation only (House3D/SUNCG, 20 train / 20 test houses), with a simple synthetic truncated-Gaussian odometry noise model the authors admit may not match real-world noise; doors are removed in the main setting.
With accurate pose, classical frontier exploration still gives higher coverage; the learned policy's advantage is robustness, not raw efficiency.
Downstream evaluation is simplistic (nearest-neighbour image localization + shortest-path planner, no noise), and most results are reported only as curves.
builds_on: Cognitive Mapping and Planning (egocentric spatial memory)
compares_to: Curiosity-driven exploration (Pathak et al. 2017, Burda et al. 2019 variant)
